title: Boeing Reports Loss on $280 Million Hit to Troubled Air Force One Program
partialText: Boeing pushed back delivery of two presidential planes by four years. The delay and related expenses contributed to a bigger-than-expected loss in the second quarter.

title: Prediction Market Betting on Drug Trials and Approvals Sparks Concern About Undermining Research
partialText: Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket now let people wager money on drug approvals. Kalshi also plans to allow bets on clinical trial results.

title: The Chips Rout Goes Global
partialText: Shares in semiconductor companies plunged in South Korea and Europe, adding fresh doubts to the durability of the artificial intelligence trade.

title: Public Control or ‘20th-Century Socialism’? U.K. Debates a Different Way.
partialText: The new prime minister, Andy Burnham, faulted Margaret Thatcher’s privatization in the 1980s. He wants an alternative economic model, especially to run utilities.

title: Police Say Binance Is Making It Harder to Fight Crime
partialText: Investigators in Europe said that the cryptocurrency giant Binance had made it more difficult to track down scammers and solve other crimes.

title: Faith and Kenny Lattimore Chose a Rare Move: Fighting Defamation on YouTube
partialText: Faith Jenkins Lattimore and Kenny Lattimore took the rare step of battling defamation on YouTube. Even with money and legal experience, they struggled to make progress.

title: To Recruit Teachers, School Districts Are Building Homes
partialText: The nation’s housing shortage has made it challenging for some essential workers like educators to live where they work. An increasing number of school districts are trying to change that.

title: Tech Stocks Tumble on Worries Over A.I. Spending and China’s Chips
partialText: The Nasdaq Composite index fell over 1 percent when markets opened in the United States, following deep declines across Asia earlier in the day.

title: He Served China’s Police State of Xinjiang. He Says It Imprisoned Him, Too.
partialText: After nearly 10 years carrying out Chinese government repression in Xinjiang, a former police officer is now seeking asylum in Germany.

title: Minnesota Judge Blocks First State Ban on Prediction Markets Like Kalshi and Polymarket
partialText: The law, which would make it a felony for most prediction markets to operate and advertise in the state, was set to take effect on Saturday.

title: BuzzFeed Lays Off a Third of Its Staff
partialText: The company’s new owner, Byron Allen, is cutting roughly 180 employees as he looks to reduce its financial losses.

title: Chinese Start-Up Moonshot Details New A.I. Model
partialText: Moonshot said some users would have to get licenses to use its Kimi K3 model as the company threads a needle between sharing and profiting from its technology’s popularity.

title: Julie Masino, Cracker Barrel CEO Who Oversaw Logo Change, Steps Down
partialText: Julie Masino faced backlash online when the company tried to shed its old-timey image. David Deno, a former chief of Bloomin’ Brands, will take over.

title: Even China’s A.I. Powerhouses Can’t Figure Out How to Profit Off A.I.
partialText: Chinese A.I. models are gaining ground. But the companies behind them do not have a clear strategy to make money from that success.

title: Why Restarting a Nuclear Power Plant Can Be Much Harder Than Expected
partialText: The first U.S. attempt at reopening a shuttered reactor has been held back by run-down equipment and a lack of planning.

title: The A.I. Debate That’s Driving a Wedge Through Big Tech
partialText: Investors and policymakers must contend with the competing camps that view open and closed artificial intelligence models as key to the sector’s future.

title: 5 New Hotels in Vintage Buildings
partialText: From a restored warehouse in Seattle to a former prison in Nara, Japan, these accommodations offer intriguing surroundings with modern comforts.

title: The Fed’s New Chairman Faces His Biggest Test Yet
partialText: Kevin M. Warsh, who has said the Federal Reserve has “no tolerance” for elevated inflation, must decide whether he wants to push for an interest-rate increase at this week’s policy meeting.

title: 5 Things to Know About Meta’s Giant Data Center in Louisiana
partialText: The road to the giant project was paved with secret meetings and an ever-expanding building plan.

title: Paramount is Betting Johnny Depp Can Make a Comeback With ‘Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol’
partialText: Paramount is betting that audiences will re-embrace the star a decade after allegations of domestic abuse and a defamation trial.

title: How Meta Got Everything It Wanted in a Secret Louisiana Data Center Deal
partialText: A Times examination details how the Silicon Valley giant used private talks with local officials to start a project big enough to cover nearly six square miles.

title: China’s CXMT Stock Soars 470% in Start of Trading, Amid A.I. Race
partialText: The meteoric rise on its first day of trading catapulted CXMT, China’s leading memory chipmaker, to being the most valuable company on the Shanghai stock exchange.

title: Iran War Forces Energy Buyers to ‘Unshackle’ From Global Markets
partialText: Developing Asian nations, scarred by Middle East supply shocks, are working to scale back their reliance on imported fuels, including liquefied natural gas.

title: Oil Prices Sink After U.S. and Iran Pause Fighting a Second Day
partialText: No strikes have been reported from either side since Friday, leaving oil investors optimistic about a resolution to the conflict.

title: Why Paramount Paused Its Blockbuster $111 Billion Deal for Warner Bros.
partialText: A flurry of negotiations last week cleared the way for an antitrust court battle with states that could determine the fate of the two iconic media giants.

title: Kids (and Adults) Are Obsessed With Squishy Toys and Fidget Trading
partialText: Kids are making, trading and hunting for squishies, or squeezable, malleable blob toys that come in a variety of forms.

title: A Son of Wealth Finds His Calling in a High-End Grocery Store
partialText: How the scion Sammy Nussdorf found his calling among the carefully arranged shelves of Meadow Lane, his chic market in Lower Manhattan.

title: Meet Jeffrey Epstein’s Girlfriend, Who Stands to Inherit Much of His Estate
partialText: Karyna Shuliak, 37, is a complicated and unusual figure in the disgraced financier’s world who has been trying to blend into obscurity since his death.

title: How the Prius Traces Its Lineage to a 1900 Car From Ferdinand Porsche
partialText: The Lohner-Porsche Semper Vivus had a generator that recharged a battery, and it even had regenerative braking. Sound familiar?

title: Sell the Company for $400 Million? He’s Giving It Away Instead.
partialText: After his sole heir died, Eddie Smith, the owner of Grady-White Boats, looked for a way to pass on his legacy. He was inspired by Patagonia to pledge future profits to charity.

title: Blockbuster I.P.O.s Are Creating New Millionaires. Philanthropies Want a Cut.
partialText: As start-ups like Anthropic and OpenAI prepare to go public, nonprofits are hoping for a secondary giving windfall from the new tech ultrawealthy.

title: Tankers Sail Through Red Sea Despite Houthi Blockade
partialText: Dozens of ships continued to traverse the Red Sea this week, but with scattered disruption, uncertainty about the passage grows by the hour.

title: A Global Economy Jolted by an Oil Shock Now Gets a Tariff Reminder
partialText: Tariffs are back, but this time there is a war in the Persian Gulf and oil has hit $100 a barrel.

title: 1.6 Million Egg Cartons Are Recalled Over Salmonella Risk
partialText: The voluntary recall included eggs produced in Texas and sold under several brand names in six states, the Food and Drug Administration said.

title: Trump to Speak as White House Correspondents Dinner Returns With More Security
partialText: President Trump remains the evening’s keynote speaker, as relations between his administration and the press continue to deteriorate.

title: F.D.A. Panel’s Vote on Peptides Raises Concerns About a Prescribing Boom
partialText: The committee endorsed broader use of the peptides in lightly regulated compounding pharmacies that have grown into a multibillion-dollar business.

title: Paramount Agrees to Delay Warner Bros. Merger for Months
partialText: The company agreed to a proposed freeze until June 2027, unless a judge issues a ruling before then on a lawsuit blocking the deal.

title: Trump Administration Admits Canceling Grants to States That Did Not Vote for Him
partialText: Federal officials said in court documents that they halted billions of dollars in funding for energy projects to states “based solely” on whether they backed President Trump in the 2024 election.

title: Small Businesses Sue Trump Administration Over Latest Tariffs
partialText: The businesses are represented by the Liberty Justice Center, a legal group that has successfully challenged President Trump’s past duties.

partialText: Cecilia Vega described what she said was pressure from executives to insert bias into several segments that aired this year.

partialText: After the soda company introduced a new brand design, some fans spotted similarities to the typeface used by the cigarette brand. Enter the font nerds.

title: China Has Come Through Trump’s Trade War in a Good Position
partialText: Despite threats from President Trump, the overall average weighted tariff on Chinese goods remained about the same.

title: Crucial Interest Rate Jumps to Highest Level of Trump’s Second Term
partialText: The yield on the 10-year Treasury bond has risen steadily this year, as the Iran war rages, government spending worries intensify and artificial intelligence spending boosts growth.

title: Clock Ticks Down to Europe’s Ban on Russian Gas Tankers
partialText: Europeans say they fear a rising dependence on American energy even with a Jan. 1 deadline to end liquefied natural gas imports from Russia.

title: China Wields Its Rare Earth Leverage Over Europe With New Export Controls
partialText: Beijing banned shipments of important supplies to 14 companies on the cutting edge of chemicals processing, electric motors and defense.

partialText: Creditors are going after past-due credit card and other debts as Americans are strapped by higher prices. New legal protections and A.I. could help.

title: Why It’s Best to Keep Politics Out of Your Investment Strategy
partialText: Despite the blurring of lines between big business and the Trump administration, investing in broad index funds instead of stocks with political ties looks like a better bet.

partialText: Households and businesses were already contending with an affordability crunch. A new round of tariffs could inflict more pain.

partialText: As renewed fighting with Iran sends oil and gas prices soaring, President Trump has imposed new global tariffs that could push up prices further.

title: Is the Amaury Family, Owners of the Tour de France, Hurting Cycling?
partialText: The Amaurys of Paris own the race, but won’t share any of the $170 million in media revenue. Sponsors and riders say their resistance is dooming the sport.
